elaboration_control.just_in_time_note: F3.2 and F2.1 are on the roadmap and were not elaborated. Elaborating them now would produce stories against a feature definition the next cycle plan may change, which is the waste just-in-time exists to avoid.

slicing_decisions.rationale: The collapsible-story rule: a story is only a vertical slice of an oversized feature. F5.1 fits one cycle, so no slice layer is created and its acceptance criteria carry forward unchanged for Work-Unit elaboration. Minting a story here would add a level that restates the feature and nothing else.

slicing_decisions.fit_test: size L — does not fit one feature cycle
slicing_decisions.rationale: Two independently valuable vertical slices exist: a producer can register and be held pending (a) before asynchronous verification resolves the outcome (b). Each slice re-runs the fit test on its own.

stories.title: Happy-path producer registration
stories.narrative: As a producer, I want to submit my registration with my FBO number so that I can begin the process of listing produce.

fit_test.basis: one cycle; a demonstrable end-to-end path from form submission to a pending record

stories.depends_on_features_note: A producer cannot register before there is an authenticated external identity to register as. F5.1 is committed to the same cycle and ranked ahead of it (wsjf_rank 1 vs 3).

acceptance_criteria.given: an authenticated producer on the registration form
acceptance_criteria.when: they submit a well-formed FBO number
acceptance_criteria.then: the registration is accepted and held with status pending-verification

acceptance_criteria.given: an authenticated producer on the registration form
acceptance_criteria.when: they submit a malformed FBO number
acceptance_criteria.then: the submission is refused with a field-level message and no registration record is created

acceptance_criteria.when: they submit without having ticked the FBO-status attestation
acceptance_criteria.then: the submission is refused server-side, and the refusal is not bypassable by altering the client request

acceptance_criteria.given: a producer with a registration held pending-verification
acceptance_criteria.when: they attempt to publish a listing
acceptance_criteria.then: publication is blocked and the producer is told verification is still in progress

out_of_scope: The outcome of the FBO lookup itself — that is S-F1.1-b
stories.domain_notes: FBO = Food Business Operator; the party legally accountable for a food product at a point in the chain. An unverified producer is never merely 'not yet shown' — they are blocked from publishing, because publication is the point of sale.

stories.title: Asynchronous FBO verification and its outcomes
stories.narrative: As a compliance-accountable platform, I want a producer's declared FBO registration verified against the competent authority's register so that no unverified party can sell.

fit_test.basis: one cycle; both outcome paths are demonstrable against a stubbed register

acceptance_criteria.when: the FBO lookup returns a valid status
acceptance_criteria.then: the registration becomes valid, the verification is recorded as evidence, and publication is permitted

acceptance_criteria.when: the FBO lookup returns an invalid status
acceptance_criteria.then: the registration is rejected, the producer is notified with the reason, and publication stays blocked

acceptance_criteria.when: the FBO lookup does not answer within its timeout
acceptance_criteria.then: the registration stays pending and is retried; it is never optimistically treated as valid
acceptance_criteria.citation: kb-L2-food-domain (an unknown eligibility is a refusal or a deferral, never an optimistic assumption)

acceptance_criteria.when: the same verification event is delivered a second time
acceptance_criteria.then: no second verification record is created
acceptance_criteria.citation: kb-L2-food-domain (evidence events carry a deduplication key derived from the business act; a replay asserts the fact twice)

out_of_scope: Re-verification on registration expiry — no committed requirement covers it; raised as OQ-01
stories.domain_notes: The verification record is regulatory evidence, not application state: it may be produced in a dispute years later, so it is append-only and a duplicate assertion is a compliance defect rather than a cosmetic one.

stories.title: External identity-provider integration
stories.narrative_note: No narrative and no slice id: F5.1 was not sliced. This record exists so the feature's acceptance criteria reach the task generator in one place, not to introduce a story level the fit test said was unnecessary.

fit_test.basis: size M; fits one cycle without slicing

acceptance_criteria.when: they authenticate through the group-approved external identity provider
acceptance_criteria.then: a session is established and no employee-directory credential is involved
acceptance_criteria.citation: kb-L1-enterprise-security § ES1 (the employee directory has no external-party tier)

acceptance_criteria.given: an authenticated external party with no role claim
acceptance_criteria.then: the party is provisioned with the role their onboarding record specifies, and no default elevated role is granted
the call is refused server-side and the refusal is not bypassable by altering the client request

coverage.rationale: Unsliced: the feature's three AC carry forward verbatim, same ids, none invented.

Sliced: each of F1.1's four AC is claimed by exactly one slice, and each slice added the negative and duplicate-delivery cases its own fit test needs. Every added AC traces to a parent AC and an FR — none is a new requirement wearing an AC's clothes.

pii_detection.note: No personal data appears in any narrative, acceptance criterion or example value. Two draft AC carried a sample producer name and a sample FBO number; both were replaced with role placeholders ('an authenticated producer') and a format description ('a well-formed FBO number') rather than a specimen value. A realistic-looking registration number in an AC is indistinguishable from a real one to everything downstream that reads it.

citation_verifier.note: Every claim not derivable from the feature AC itself carries a citation to its source. The two domain claims — refusal on an unknown eligibility, and deduplication of evidence events — cite kb-L2-food-domain rather than being asserted as general good practice.

open_questions.question: What happens when a previously verified FBO registration lapses or is revoked after the producer has published listings?
open_questions.note: FR-003 covers verification before first publication and is silent on continuous validity. Not invented into an acceptance criterion; the slice states it as out of scope.

open_questions.question: Is the competent-authority register queried live, or is a periodically refreshed copy acceptable?
open_questions.note: Affects whether the Work Unit is an integration against a live service or against a cached dataset — a difference the task generator cannot resolve on its own.

artifacts.name: stories.json
artifacts.description: Cycle 1 elaboration: 2 story slices under F1.1 plus F5.1 carried unsliced; 15 acceptance criteria, all traced to FR-001, FR-003 or FR-005

content.execution_summary:
• Elaborated 2 committed features into 3 records: 2 story slices (S-F1.1-a, S-F1.1-b) and F5.1 carried forward unsliced.
• Collapsible-story rule applied in both directions. F5.1 (needs_slicing=false) got NO story layer — a story there would have restated the feature and added a level. F1.1 (needs_slicing=true, size L) got two slices, each of which independently re-passed the fit test.
• 15 acceptance criteria in Given/When/Then. 7 carried verbatim from the feature AC with their ids intact; 8 added by slicing, each tracing to a parent AC and an FR. No AC introduces a requirement that no FR supports.
• Requirement coverage: FR-001, FR-003, FR-005 all covered. Slice ordering is stated (S-F1.1-a before S-F1.1-b) along with F1.1's cross-feature dependency on F5.1 — a producer cannot register before there is an identity to register as.
• Just-in-time honoured: F3.2 and F2.1 are on the roadmap and were deliberately not elaborated.
• Open questions: 2 — OQ-01 (registration lapse after publication) and OQ-02 (live register vs cached copy). Both are genuine gaps and are recorded as out-of-scope rather than resolved into an acceptance criterion the requirements do not support.
• Knowledge bases consulted: kb-L1-sdlc-templates (Definition of Ready, AC form); kb-L2-food-domain (FBO meaning, refusal-on-unknown-eligibility, evidence-event deduplication).
• Guardrails evaluated: gr-L1-schema-validator (pass), gr-L1-pii-detection (pass — two specimen values replaced with placeholders before emission), gr-L1-citation-verifier (pass — 7 cited claims, 0 uncited).
• Next: scenario-writer, adversarial-case-writer and case-writer mint case_ids against these acceptance criteria; task-generator then binds those case_ids as verification_ref.
